page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.6xlarge is a storage-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz, providing 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor architecture includes a 320 MB L3 cache and supports specialized instruction sets, including AVX-512 extensions and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance features 192.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory (6 GHz), delivering an 8:1 memory-to-core allocation (8.0 GB per vCPU). Additionally, it bundles 15,000 GB of dense local NVMe SSD storage and provides 25 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth without discrete GPUs.

Benchmark data demonstrates competitive single-thread responsiveness and high memory write throughput. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a top-tier single-core score of 2314.0 alongside a strong multi-core score of 16504.0. Uncached large-block memory writes reached 107.16 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% of measured instances. The server also delivered strong throughput in single-threaded gzip compression (34.65 GB/sec), image processing, and static web serving (45.64 GB/sec). Small-model LLM text generation (135M parameters) ranked in the top 10% at 415.29 tokens per second, aided by AMX acceleration. In contrast, multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU scores, and PassMark database operations fell within mid-tier performance percentiles.

The dense hardware configuration provides solid cost efficiency for architectures demanding significant local non-volatile storage paired with high memory capacity. Rather than scaling out across multiple smaller nodes, the integration of 15 TB of NVMe SSD directly into the host reduces remote storage I/O bottlenecks and simplifies operational complexity. However, workloads requiring massive parallel compute or hardware GPU acceleration may find the 24-vCPU ceiling limiting.

AWS i7ie.6xlarge is suited for I/O-intensive and data-heavy operations. Its profile fits high-throughput transactional and analytical databases, large distributed storage nodes, in-memory caching platforms with persistent local logs, and real-time data ingestion pipelines.
